decisions.reason: The firm has already invested in and publicly committed to this camera with a dedicated product presence, it fits the core optical navigation and observation business, and in long space procurement cycles any weak traction can still be interpreted as temporary.

This product should be kept because it is close to the core business, has sustained public visibility, and the reported ESA HERA mission success strongly reinforces management’s commitment to continue backing it.

Management would keep this sensor suite because it extends the established offer into a strategically important adjacent field, has been visibly presented to the market, and disappointing results could still be justified as timing-related in a slowly maturing space market.

Even with lower website prominence, the firm is likely to persist because a miniaturized space-qualified LiDAR sensor matches its announced direction toward compact future spacecraft sensors and sunk development effort encourages continuation.

This recently launched radiation-hard camera fits the firm’s heritage and quality positioning, has already received a dedicated market presentation, and is too aligned with the public strategy to abandon after such an early period.

Although still only lightly presented, this asteroid navigation and imaging camera builds on the firm’s established capabilities and is recent enough that management can plausibly attribute any limited market evidence to normal mission-cycle delays rather than product failure.
